data.title: Why Is Penny Stock CVD Equipment (CVV) Down Today?
data.description:
CVD Equipment (CVV) stock took a beating on Friday following an update on the engineering and manufacturing company's operations. The company said it will stop seeking new system orders for its CVD equipment business as part of a new restructuring plan. The company will cut its workforce by about half. The move will leave enough staff to finish its current backlog, meet warranty needs and run its spare parts, quartz and services business. CVD Equipment expects a charge of about $0.8 million to $1.0 million this quarter.

The plan will also bring a change to CVD Equipment leadership. Emmanuel Lakios left his roles as president and CEO on September 3 and will no longer sit on the Board. Warren Cheesman, CVD Equipment's vice president of manufacturing operations, has been named acting CEO. The Board said it will keep looking at ways to cut costs, sell assets and boost value, with its Central Islip site among the assets under review.

"In light of continued weakness in prospective equipment order activity, declining backlog, the CVD equipment division's ongoing operating losses, and the lack of viable strategic alternatives for the business, we have decided to discontinue the pursuit of new equipment system orders," said Lawrence Waldman, CVD Equipment's chairman. He said the plan is meant to lower costs and risk while helping the company keep cash on hand.

The company will now focus on its existing orders and its parts, quartz and service work. Cheesman said the company will focus on careful use of its assets and cash while it works to meet its customer needs. The board will also assess other business paths that fit its resources and goals.

data.title: SOUN Stock Price Forecast: Can SoundHound Hit $20?
data.description:
SoundHound AI (SOUN) stock is down about 36% year-to-date as investors weigh its growth outlook against ongoing losses and a high valuation. Still, Wall Street remains bullish, with H.C. Wainwright analyst Scott Buck holding a Street-high $20 price target. At recent levels, that target implies more than 200% upside. Meanwhile, the average analyst target of $12 implies about 90% upside.

SoundHound AI focuses on voice recognition and natural language processing, providing AI-powered solutions for multiple industries.

What Could Drive SOUN Stock Higher?

SoundHound reported record second-quarter revenue of $61.9 million, up 45% year-over-year. The company also raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $230 million to $260 million. The company is betting on demand for voice AI and its OASYS agentic AI platform, which can handle tasks such as customer service and food orders. SoundHound also signed an eight-figure deal within 90 days of launching the platform.

The planned LivePerson (LPSN) acquisition could add another growth driver. SoundHound expects the combined business to reach $350 million to $400 million in annual revenue once the deal is fully integrated.

SoundHound's growth is still coming at a cost. The company posted a $42.8 million GAAP net loss in Q2 and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $9.6 million. The company also used $60 million in operating cash during the first half of 2026.

There are other risks to the growth story. A slowdown in enterprise tech spending could hurt demand for SoundHound's voice AI tools. The company also faces strong competition in the space. If growth slows, SOUN stock could see a sharp pullback.

SOUN's Street-High Price Target

Buck expects the company to reach adjusted EBITDA break-even by the end of 2026 while continuing to invest in growth. Although this could pressure near-term profits, he believes it will drive long-term growth. Earlier, Buck stated that SoundHound AI is growing its partner base, which could help bring in new customers and lift revenue.

Overall, Buck's case rests on SoundHound's strong revenue growth and progress toward adjusted EBITDA break-even. The main risk is whether the company can turn that growth into sustained profits.

data.title: Wedbush Says Buy CRWD, PANW, and DDOG Stocks. Here's What's Driving the Optimism
data.description:
Wedbush analyst Steven Wahrhaftig initiated coverage on CrowdStrike (CRWD), Palo Alto Networks (PANW), and Datadog (DDOG) with Buy ratings, given their solid growth and a strong demand backdrop. Cybersecurity companies are benefiting from the rising threat of cyberattacks amid growing AI adoption. After trending higher in Friday's pre-market trading, all three stocks were in the red at the time of writing.

Here's Why Wedbush Is Bullish on CRWD Stock

Wahrhaftig assigned CrowdStrike a price target of $250 based on FY29 EV/FCF of 85x and an EV/Revenue multiple of nearly 29x. The analyst highlighted the company's accelerating ARR (annual recurring revenue), solid net new ARR, and revenue growth in Q2 FY27, along with strong margins.

Wahrhaftig also noted the strong demand for CRWD's Falcon platform in AI-native endpoint protection and its multi-year growth potential as it expands into cloud, identity, and security information and event management (SIEM).

Wahrhaftig also noted that growth in cloud-native and AI-native workloads is boosting demand for observability, positioning Datadog as a leading pure-play provider. He added that the company is investing heavily in research and development (R&D) to expand its product portfolio, adding over 100 new capabilities announced at its DASH 2026 keynote in June. data.title: Eli Lilly Stock (LLY) in Focus as Company Completes $3.8 Billion AtaiBeckley Purchase
data.description:
U.S. pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly (LLY) has announced that it completed its acquisition of AtaiBeckley, a biopharmaceutical company developing treatments for mental health conditions. The deal is valued at $3.8 billion and provides Eli Lilly therapies for the treatment of clinical depression and other mental health conditions.

Eli Lilly has said that the acquisition of AtaiBeckley should boost its neuroscience portfolio. Eli Lilly agreed to pay $6.75 per share in cash for AtaiBeckley earlier this year, representing $2.8 billion. An additional payment of about $1 billion could be paid by Eli Lilly if AtaiBeckley reaches certain clinical trial, regulatory, and commercialization milestones, bringing the transactions total potential value to $3.8 billion.

Eli Lily's Growth Strategy

The purchase of AtaiBeckley continues Eli Lilly's strategy of growing through acquisitions. The company has been building its pipeline of potential new drugs by acquiring smaller pharmaceutical companies and biotechnology startups. Eli Lilly has spent about $35 billion on corporate buyouts and acquisitions since 2020.

data.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman Says Company Willing to Slow AI Development
data.description:
Responding to a growing backlash, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has told employees that the startup company is willing to slow its artificial intelligence (AI) development. Speaking at a company meeting, Altman reportedly said that the firm ‌is open to slowing development of its AI systems. The comments come amid rising concerns about the safety ​of AI and a public backlash to data centers.

Altman told staff that the ChatGPT maker could slow its pace of development to match other AI companies. Earlier in the week, several ⁠AI researchers issued stark warnings about the dangers of AI technologies. Jacob Coxon, a former OpenAI researcher, publicly accused the company of racing ​toward AI advancements without acting ​responsibly.

Worse, Evan Hubinger, a safety researcher at OpenAI rival Anthropic, warned that AI is advancing so quickly tat there is a greater than 10% chance it "could kill all humans" within a decade.

data.title: Oracle's Q1 Beat Has Analysts Bullish but Cautious on ORCL Stock. Is It a Buy?
data.description:
Oracle's (ORCL) fiscal first-quarter results came in ahead of Wall Street expectations, sending shares up 6% in premarket trading, but analysts are offering mixed views on the stock. Strong cloud growth and a sharp increase in remaining performance obligations (RPO) helped offset concerns around margins and cash flow.

Revenue rose 30% year-over-year to $19.34 billion, topping the $19.13 billion consensus estimate, while adjusted EPS came in at $1.92 versus expectations of $1.74.

OCI Growth Accelerates

The strongest part of the quarter was Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), where growth accelerated to 121% from 93% in the previous quarter. RPO, which represents contracted revenue yet to be recognized, reached $664 billion, up $209 billion year-over-year and above the $618 billion consensus estimate. Oracle also raised its FY27 revenue guidance to more than $90 billion, with management expecting OCI revenue growth of roughly 120%.

Promotion

ORCZ: built for a short position on ORCL

Barclays Sees Further Upside

Barclays analyst Raimo Lenschow raised his price target to $252 from $250 and maintained a Buy rating. Lenschow believes Oracle's growth has reached an inflection point and should accelerate further. He also highlighted the completion of Oracle's $20 billion at-the-market equity raise, which improves the company's funding position and addresses concerns around its large AI infrastructure investments.

Stifel Flags Margin Pressure

Stifel analyst Brad Reback took a more cautious view, cutting his price target to $200 from $220 while maintaining a Buy rating. Reback acknowledged the strong quarter and accelerating OCI growth but pointed to lower near-term gross margins. Still, he expects improving operating expenses and stronger OCI growth to support EPS expansion over the coming years.

RBC Maintains a Hold

RBC Capital analyst Rishi Jaluria lowered his price target on Oracle to $165 from $190 while maintaining a Hold rating. The firm acknowledged Oracle's strong Q1 results but remains cautious about lower margins and heavy infrastructure spending.

Oppenheimer Sees Financing Relief

Oppenheimer analyst Brian Schwartz reiterated a Buy rating and $275 price target, citing accelerating OCI growth, faster capacity delivery, and infrastructure demand continuing to exceed supply. He expects Oracle's leaner cost base to help offset AI-driven margin pressure.

However, Schwartz flagged persistent gross margin compression, normalized net-new RPO, and increasing reliance on customer prepayments. The completion of the ATM equity raise also helped ease financing concerns.

Is ORCL Stock a Good Buy?

On TipRanks, ORCL has a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 21 Buys and four Hold ratings. The average Oracle price target of $257.76 implies 68.5% upside potential from current levels. Year-to-date, ORCL shares have dropped 20.8%.
